clinician.trajectory_summary: A 21-year-old woman presented with subjective visual impairment and blurry vision for 3 weeks. Initial ophthalmological examinations were normal. Six weeks after initial symptoms, she developed lower limb weakness and clinical transverse myelitis. Spinal cord MRI revealed lesions extending over 3 vertebral segments, and brain MRI showed 3 lesions not meeting diagnostic criteria for multiple sclerosis. The patient was treated with IV steroids. NMO-IgG seropositive status was confirmed. Over 4 years of observation, visual function remained good, but urinary incontinence and walking disorders worsened.

Long-term follow-up showed good visual function but worsening urinary incontinence and walking disorders.
